title: Thresholding Error Bounded by Squared Uniform Norm
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $g$ be a real-valued function on that cube, and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$. If the square of the uniform $L^2$ norm of the difference between the real-valued version of $f$ and $g$ is at most $\varepsilon$, then the relative Hamming distance from $f$ to the function obtained by thresholding $g$ at zero (assigning zero the sign $+1$) is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
